newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Nordbanken says state could publicly sell holding.
newsitem.headline: Nordbanken says state could publicly sell holding.

text.p: Nordbanken chairman Jacob Palmstierna said on Wednesday a broad-based public offering was the only possibility for the state to sell its stake in commercial bank Nordbanken.
"We don't see a single bid for the whole bank as a possibility in the near future ... the only possibility is to hold a wide share offering," Palmstierna told reporters.
Sweden's state-controlled Nordbanken on Wednesday proposed a five billion crown share buy-back that could reduce the government's holding to 58 percent from 65.5 percent.
He said the state's holding after a buy-out could be sold all at once.
"After the buy-out it's not improbable that the market would allow that," Palmstierna said.
He said the bank would talk with the Finance Department about when the sale would take place but any final decision would be a job for the finance minister.
He could not elaborate on when a decision would be made.
"There is no concrete timetable," Palmstierna said.

Swedish Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said the government supported the buyback proposal, saying it would improve the health of the bank and also permit the government to reduce its stake in the bank.
